notes: Settled: one dossier for Cliopatria's single row 'Yan' (-750..-204), extended back to the c. 1046 Zhou enfeoffment and forward to Zang Tu's capture in 202. Wikidata Q1472004 is shared with Former Yan (a 4th-century CE Xianbei state), a different state: not merged. Year numbering: the ledger uses the BC number negated; Cliopatria's last Warring States Yan year is -223 while the pages say 222 BC, and its Song ends -285 against 286 BC, so Cliopatria may use astronomical years (1 BC = 0); the orchestrator should check before rendering, since every BC date here could be a year off against the shapes. Repair (reviewer fail, 2026-10-18): Cliopatria's Yan shapes of 404, 291 and 208 all begin at 116.70E and leave out a 60-cell block (about 10,400 km2, 115.9-117.1E, 38.6-40.1N) that the 750 shape holds and that contains the capital Ji; the block is restored in yan_-404, yan_-300, yan_-291, yan_-209 and yan_-208, the 'loss to Zhao 404' line is deleted (the Zhao page names no Yan loss), and the Ji block is added to the 226 loss and the 209 gain. Cliopatria's rows over the block (Zhao 404, 59 cells; Zhongshan 366-301, 59; Wei 291, 58; Qin 222, 58; Zhai 208, 50; Dai 208, 8) are therefore wrong over Ji for the years Yan held it: the Zhao, Zhongshan, Wei, Qin, Zhai and Dai groups should check them (the Zhao page does say Zhao annexed some Yan territory, undated and unplaced, so part of the block may have changed hands later). The State of Ji (Beijing) is cut from the shape until the 7th-century absorption (placeholder -650; the Ji page gives no year). The enlarged Yan (Liaodong and the Donghu land) is drawn from 300, as the Qin Kai ('around 300 BC') and Donghu people ('In 300 BCE') pages date it, not from Cliopatria's 291. Han Guang's Yan starts in 209 (Han Guang page infobox 'King of Yan 209 BC - 206 BC'), one year before Cliopatria's revived shape. The 5 cells Cliopatria gives the Xiongnu in 208 are on no page (Modu Chanyu page: no Yan land); no loss is recorded. Unsettled: (1) the end year of the Qi occupation (312 on the Yan list, 311 on the King Zhao page; neither page dates the revolt); (2) Xiadu is undated and lies outside every Cliopatria Yan shape (the page says Yi County, Baoding; its coordinates on the page, 39.617N 116.056E, do not fit Yi County, so no circle was added); (3) the extent of the Donghu land and the dates of the Great Wall of Yan and the five commanderies (the Yan page: 'At the turn of the 3rd century BC'); (4) Zhao-Yan wars (undated); (5) the State of Ji and the Donghu need dossiers or stay names (counterparts 'Ji (state)' and 'Donghu'); (6) 'liaodong' (ea-02) overlaps Yan from 206 per the Zang Tu page and should end in 206; the Qi dossier has no 314 BC occupation of Yan and no mirror of the Gojoseon loss c. 300 (gojoseon starts in Cliopatria only in 197). Gazetteer: no unknown names are used; the capitals are plain coordinates.
